summary: The root م-ع-ي primarily signifies being with someone or something, indicating companionship, presence, or association. It can also denote support or agreement, implying a shared state or action.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: مِعًى A narrow, depressed place (See طَأْطَاءٌ.) بَنَاتٌ مِعًى The بَعْر. (T in art. بنى.) المِعَى المُسْتَقِيمُ The rectum.

الأَمْعَاءُ i. q. الأَقْصَابُ; (AO: see voce قِتْبٌ;) the guts; i. e. bowels, or intestines, into which the food passes from the stomach: الحَشَا is the name of all the places of the food; and in the belly are the أَعْفَاج and the أَقْتَاب, to which the food passes after the stomach, and these are the lower امعاء; and all these are called the قُصْب: the حَوَايَا are all the امعاء that wind, or take a coiled, or circular, form. (Zj, in his “ Khalk el-Insán.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
